correctness.rationale: Source step (2.3) with L=0 yields exact scalar recurrence; two explicit steps give b=-2C/a and the coefficient K. The ratio bound tA(x)/x² on a compact nonzero interval, r2=O(t²) and a geometric tail prove all future iterates stay away from the minimizer and converge to x∞. Exact rational and square-root bounds at a=C=1, h=20 independently enclose the full infinite orbit. The embedded checker passed its finite arithmetic and trajectory checks; finite tests are not used to prove asymptotics.

value.rationale: The result resolves a structural gap between a modified-energy certificate and the actual first-order stationarity objective on the simplest strongly convex problem. The reciprocal x∞=-2C/a and sharp first correction determine an observable failure location for every nonzero initialization when h is large, while the exact h=20 witness makes the phenomenon rigorously reproducible. This diagnoses why auxiliary consistency control matters without claiming wider convergence barriers.
